concepts.learning_objective: Describe an algorithm as a precise step-by-step procedure built from basic steps.
Execute and justify the right-to-left column addition algorithm with a carry.
Compare the effort of counting dots with the effort of adding column by column.

topics.title: Computing the divisors of a number

concepts.learning_objective: Execute the algorithm that builds the list of divisors of n by checking each j from 1 to n.
Use the pairing of divisors to reduce the numbers that must be examined.

topics.title: Finding the gcd from common divisors

concepts.learning_objective: Build the list of common divisors of two numbers from their lists of divisors.
Explain why the rightmost element of the common-divisors list is the gcd.

topics.title: Data structures and improving the gcd algorithm

concepts.learning_objective: Recognise a list as a data structure that stores named intermediate values.
Refine the gcd algorithm by combining scans, scanning up to min(m, n) and dropping lists.
Analyse how the work of the scanning gcd algorithm grows with the size of the numbers.
Justify that gcd(m, n) = gcd(n, m - n) when m is at least n.
Execute Euclid's subtraction algorithm, including the reversal and stopping steps.
Evaluate why the subtraction algorithm can need many steps for inputs like gcd(2k + 1, 2).

topics.title: Aryabhata's division algorithm and the history of the word

concepts.learning_objective: Use the reduction gcd(m, n) = gcd(n, m mod n) to compute a gcd in few steps.
Carry out the long-division layout for the gcd and read off the answer.
Recall how the word algorithm arose from Al-Khwarizmi and Indian arithmetic.
